steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Look at the level of detail. This guy could even imitate expressions and mouth movements.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Let me see inside your mouth. Aaah...

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: (Opens mouth)

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Hmm. I can see structures resembling vocal cords. So why haven't you said a single thing?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Speech is just movement of the vocal cords and associated muscles. You should be able to emulate it...
Pepe approaches the mummy and places her hand on its throat. The mummy follows her movement, placing its hand on Pepe's throat.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You know...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You... know...

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: Yo... oo... no... oo...
Pepe draws her hand back, covering her mouth in amazement, wonder in her eyes.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: So you CAN speak...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Inconceivable... the artificers of the Shah's time were amazing...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Right. I once read about that in Artifacts of the Old Calendar Era...

spans.text: Right. I once read about that in
Artifacts of the Old Calendar Era

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: There were those who could seal a consciousness in gems by etching Originium circuits on it, then place it inside a body of gold, allowing it to survive for millennia without decay.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Lost... Zhayedan technologies... the Shahanshah will be very interested...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: The trove must be somewhere deep inside your memories.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Just copying me isn't enough. You need to tell me where it is.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Let me see...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: 'First, the heart. At its first beat, we come to be. Second, the lungs. At their first breath, we come to feel.'

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: 'Third, the bowels. We fill them with food, cultivate our tongues, and develop our own likings. Fourth, the liver. We go into the night, awake and alert, for duty and obligation.'

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Fifth...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: What came fifth?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: The verse ends there...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Looks like the Arsalan researcher never found the answer.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: But you'll help me find it, won't you?
She stretches out her hand and places her fingers on the mummy's throat.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Yes, hanimefendi.

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: Yes, hanimefendi.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Stop copying me.

steps.name: Nameless Mummy
steps.text: Stop copying me.
She moves her hand from the mummy's throat to his hand and shakes it firmly. The mummy shakes her hand back.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I'll take that as a yes to our cooperation.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I'm here, Ajazi. Why aren't you at the door?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Where are you?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: (Whisper) What do you mean you don't know where you are?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: How am I supposed to go in without a pass...? Why is this office door built like a bloody vault?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: We don't have time, the evacuation's almost done!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Ajazi, is the hall window next to the curator office's window?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Yes, I know it's high.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I'll be careful.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Please be quiet in the museum. Disorder is the enemy of reason.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Do not push. The statues and murals displayed here are not protected by glass cases and can easily be...

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: As I said, this statue was almost damaged. We don't want to see that happen, of course.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: History may lie in the past, but that doesn't mean it's not of our concern. What we almost broke might be the joy of those who conquered the peaks centuries ago, or their mirth as they raised their goblets to one another.

steps.name: Lost Tourist
steps.text: How enlightening and professional...

steps.name: Lost Tourist
steps.text: ...But are you sure you need to keep carrying that statue? Along with everything else you're carrying right now?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Yes, I'm bringing it all back to where it belongs.

steps.name: Lost Tourist
steps.text: You sure take your work seriously, even when the museum is about to close.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: ...Close?

steps.name: Lost Tourist
steps.text: They announced about an emergency. Haven't you heard? It really gave us a fright!

steps.name: Lost Tourist
steps.text: That bumbling woman who was guiding us couldn't tell left from right, and I mean literally.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I do agree that certain affairs at this museum leave much to be desired.

steps.name: Lost Tourist
steps.text: She brought us to this dump, then disappeared without a trace.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I must dissent. This is no dump. It is Minoan—

steps.name: Lost Tourist
steps.text: You have no idea how scared we were when we realized we were lost.

steps.name: Lost Tourist
steps.text: We'll be trapped in here with all the ghosts, if we don't get out in time!

steps.name: Lost Tourist
steps.text: Look at that armor, that altar for live sacrifice...

steps.name: Nearly Fainting Tourist
steps.text: Yeah! That's why I never liked museums...
Aspasia catches the tourist before his head hits the floor.
Statue, clay jar, and goblet litter the floor, alongside the cannons that the Iberians used to carve open Bolívarian trade.

steps.name: Lost Tourist
steps.text: My dear! Are you alright?!

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Fainted from a panic attack, I suppose.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I have some smelling salts here that should bring him back to his senses, but I advise you to get him examined thoroughly later.
Aspasia deftly crushes the cotton-wrapped glass tube, and places a wet cotton swab in front of the tourist's nose.
As the tourist comes to his senses, she lifts him up and calmly carries him to the front of the line.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: An emergency, you say?

steps.name: Still Light-headed Tourist
steps.text: Oh... You sure have strong arms...

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Follow me, ladies and gentlemen. I will protect you, if anything happens.

steps.name: Still Light-headed Tourist
steps.text: Wow...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: *sigh* No more running around like this, alright?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I remember you. You're Lazvar's pet—

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: —Hey, no scratching! I just rescued you from the crowd! The least you could do is let me hug you for a moment or two.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Aww, you are so soft and fluffy. Where did Lazvar get you? I wanted one like you, but he wouldn't tell me what breed you were.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I didn't know why I found you so fascinating, until I realized that you looked like one of those cloudbeast statues from the Age of Shadow.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Say, since the staff are helping the visitors evacuate, and I can't have you running around the place, I'll take you to my workshop and show you the statue that's being restored.
Medjehtiqedti descends several flights of stairs, arriving at the conservation lab.
The air in the room is kept cold and dry to protect its contents. A single incandescent lamp illuminates the spacious room. Her exhales quickly turn to white fog.
The underground floor is dead quiet, the restoration staff being mobilized to help with the evacuation. She sniffs and feels her heart race.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: No worries, little guy, here's my table...
Some resin-like, gold-colored substance remains on the table: leftovers from Titi's work—repairing artifacts with Originium Arts.
But the cloudbeast statue on the table is nowhere to be seen.

steps.name: Wandering Staff
steps.text: I-I didn't see any cloudbeasts...

steps.name: Foreign Traveler
steps.text: A shadow flitted across your forehead just now, an ill omen. I fear you will meet with some misfortune soon.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: What... are you?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Did you come back to life like that old mummy?!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Hey, I didn't fix you so you could run around like Anat's research subject!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: And most certainly not to bring misfortune upon myself!

steps.name: Warehouse Custodian
steps.text: Did I hear someone scream? What happened?!

steps.name: Warehouse Custodian
steps.text: Oh, Medjehtiqedti Hanimefendi... What are you doing down here?

steps.name: Warehouse Custodian
steps.text: I thought you wouldn't be coming back for a while, with the museum being closed for the day, so I put away the artifacts under restoration...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: ...Never mind. I'm in the mood to put in some overtime today. You can go.

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: What? No sign of the visitors evacuating the southeast wing? Izaja was supposed to bring them out!

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: I have to lock the gates! The vice curator gave the emergency shutdown order personally. I don't even want to think about how bad it must be.

steps.name: Museum Ticketer
steps.text: Did anyone look inside?

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: Yeah, but they didn't see anyone. Where did Izaja take them?

steps.name: Museum Ticketer
steps.text: Why are you so quiet all of a sudden?

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: Listen...

steps.name: Museum Ticketer
steps.text: To what?

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: The wind.
A procession of a dozen people walks out the front gate into the sun.
They follow their leader—a woman carrying herself in a serene, dignified manner—in an orderly fashion.
She holds a pale-looking tourist on her shoulder, paying no heed to the wind brushing at her garment and caressing her hair, as though a statue that has stood for many years has come to life.

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: I feel like I've seen this scene before...

steps.name: Museum Ticketer
steps.text: ...I know. I've seen that statue plenty of times.

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: There's a statue in that pose?

steps.name: Museum Security
steps.text: Anyway, thank goodness, now I can lock the gates.

steps.name: Lost Tourist
steps.text: Thank you so much. Here's my card. My family runs a gem business, and you will get the VIP treatment, if you ever choose to visit.

steps.name: Passionate Tourist
steps.text: Come visit us in Yan and let me introduce you to my son! Rather handsome young man, if I do say to myself. My sister also has a daughter who just started working at the Tianshi Bureaus. She's single too, if that's your preference.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Thank you, but there is no need... I simply did what I must...
Aspasia turns around with a start.
The roll-up door is being pulled down, and security guards set up a sign that says 'Closed' in front of it.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Where's my goblet? And my clay jar and statue!

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: Where did Nana go? It's getting late.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: She's not at the guava and berry shop, or the enamel and porcelain shop, and not even her favorite celestine-laminated pipes...

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: What a waste of time. I tell you, that cloudbeast must have been eaten by that rampaging zombie at the museum.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: Oh no! How horrible!

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: It's just a pet. I'll buy you another. In fact, I'll buy you anything you want!

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: Never mind the gems—I'll buy you the entire gem trading post!

steps.name: Mysterious Animal
steps.text: (Raises head)

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: Is that a yes?

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: No, look at your feet...

steps.name: Mysterious Animal
steps.text: (Glares)

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: Pah, Lazvar's cur.

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: What are you looking at?

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: Ahem. Oh, hello there, Lazvar. I didn't see you.

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: Good timing. Let's do some business. My girl is very interested in this gem trading post.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: Wait, I never said that...

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: I have a mobile platform in east Sargon that includes extensive Originium refineries, dye factories, food processing plants...

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: I'll throw some gold and jewels on top of it. That should get the deal done, shouldn't it?

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: No, thank you, I'm not interested.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: The weight of this trading post is too much for you to understand.

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: Weight, huh... if nothing else, you've inherited your grandfather's arrogance.

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: A word of advice. Either keep a few fierce manglers to intimidate people like he did...

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: Or have your little cloudbeast greet VIPs like me. At least it knows when to grovel...

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: Ouch! Y-You bit me?

steps.name: Mysterious Animal
steps.text: (Bares teeth)

steps.name: Mysterious Animal
steps.text: Woof!

steps.name: Extravagant Man
steps.text: No! Stay away from me! Help—!

steps.name: Mysterious Animal
steps.text: Woof woof woof!

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: That will do, Woof.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: He's gone.

steps.name: Woof
steps.text: Woof!

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: You want me to pet you? Let's see... here?

steps.name: Woof
steps.text: (Licks happily)
A fowlbeast flies over and perches on the shoulder of the young trading post overseer's shoulder.
The overseer fiddles with the metal fowlbeast's mechanisms, turns its coil spring, and lets it fly.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: He's getting increasingly active.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: I'm sure you're looking forward to seeing him as I am. Mio doesn't often go out alone like this.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Maybe the man was right. I should have my cloudbeast greet important guests.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Hm... could Mio really bring him over?
